title: MB1-00383
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Haiti. He is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).
The events alleged by the claimant took place between XXXX XXXX XXXX 2010, and XXXX XXXX, 2011, the date of his arrival in Canada.
The claimant was targeted by some supporters of Michel Martelly, the current president of Haiti, because he supported a candidate of the "XXXX XXXX XXXX" party named XXXX XXXX.

The alleged persecution consisted of having his car set on fire, the theft of his motorcycle, threats to his family, and the rape of his daughter. The incidents took place on the night of XXXX XXXX to XXXX, 2010. The claimant was not present during these incidents.
The claimant's wife passed away on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011; according to the claimant, she suffered from hypertension.
After hearing the claimant's testimony and analyzing the evidence on file, the panel determines that he is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection." ANALYSIS Identity

The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction; a copy of his passport and of his Haitian national identity card seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC) are on file. Credibility

The claimant's credibility is harmed and undermined by several significant omissions and contradictions, because they directly concern the core of his allegations of fear and his refugee protection claim.

During his interview with the immigration officer, the claimant stated in particular that he fears persecution because he was accused by the supporters of Mr. Martelly of committing fraud during the elections to the benefit of a favoured candidate of René Préval, Jude Célestin. Omissions and contradictions

Moreover, this is never mentioned in his narrative. In his narrative, the claimant alleges instead that he had problems because he was part of the committee in charge of the campaign of a candidate to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.
When asked by the panel about this omission, the claimant stated that he did not understand why he had not written it in his narrative, stating that he could not explain it.
To support his refugee protection claim, the claimant submitted documents that were classified as P-1 to P-8.

During the hearing, when the panel asked the claimant whether he had contacted the police to file a complaint following the events of XXXX XXXX, 2010, he responded that he had, and he then submitted a copy of a complaint that was allegedly filed by his brother on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2010.

According to the claimant, this document was sent to him in XXXX 2010. When asked by the panel why he had not submitted this document with the others, the claimant could state only that he did not know why, that it had escaped him, and that he was not in contact with his family at that time. The panel is of the opinion that this response does not explain why the claimant did not submit this document at the same time as the others, with his refugee protection claim. The panel pointed out the preamble in his PIF, where it is indeed indicated that he must specify the steps that he allegedly took to obtain protection from an authority in his country. The fact that he did not do it in a timely manner and submitted it only at the last minute, during the hearing, also undermines the claimant's credibility.
The panel also points out that the document is a copy; the claimant does not have the original to submit.
Under the circumstances, the panel is of the opinion that this document is simply false.
In order for it to be in the file, the panel classified the copy as P-9.1 Other contradiction

In his narrative, the claimant indicates that he was part of the committee in charge of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX campaign. In his testimony, he stated that he was XXXX XXXX XXXX this man's election campaign. Furthermore, the claimant submitted a document2 in which the candidate, Mr. XXXX, indeed states that the claimant was XXXX XXXX XXXX. Not believing the allegations of the claimant, the panel is of the opinion that it is a self-serving document and therefore attaches no probative value to it. The panel is also of the opinion that the claimant adjusted his testimony during the hearing so that it was consistent with what was indicated in that document.

For all of these reasons, the panel does not believe the claimant and, as a result, his allegations of fear. The panel will therefore not address in its decision the issue of state protection or of an internal flight alternative.
To conclude on the claimant's lack of credibility, the panel points out that the Federal Court has ruled to this effect in several decisions.3

Exhibits P-6 and P-74 demonstrate that the claimant's wife passed away on XXXX XXXX, 2011. This event is obviously tragic in the panel's eyes, but since it does not believe the claimant's allegations, the panel also does not believe that this death is linked to these allegations. Furthermore, in his testimony, the claimant stated that his wife was suffering from hypertension and that it was following a hypertensive crisis that she passed away.

The panel is of the opinion that, for the purposes of section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Act, the claimant has not discharged his burden of establishing that there is a serious possibility of persecution or that, on a balance of probabilities, he would be subjected to a danger of torture, to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if he returned to his country of origin.

For the abovementioned reasons, the refugee protection claim of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is rejected. Jean-Pierre Beauquier Jean-Pierre Beauquier August 31, 2012 Date IRB translation Original language: French 1 Exhibit P-9: Copy of the complaint filed by his brother, XXXXX. 2 Exhibit P-3: Letter from XXXXXXX. 3 Aguilar v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) (2012 FC 150) No. IMM-2728-11, Date: February 3, 2012. 4 Exhibit P-6: photos of the burial of the claimant's late wife; Exhibit P-7: Death certificate of the claimant's wife. --------------- --------------- --------------- --------------- RPD File No. / No de dossier de la SPR : MB1-00383 2
